title: GTM Inference Ops Battlecard - Draft
content:
Purpose and usage notes:
This is a working battlecard + slide-deck hybrid for the Field (AE/SE) focused on inference operations conversations: cost/latency SLAs, private deployment concerns, and migration/cost-savings proof points.

Quick context (TL;DR):
- Audience: Platform engineering, ML infra leads, SRE, and product teams evaluating inference platforms.
- Objective: Equip field with concise talking points, measurable win themes, competitor rebuttals, and a short deck to share in discovery calls.
- Status: Draft v2 — needs validation from Applied ML and Pricing before we promote to 'in_review'.

Slide 1: Opening — value summary (title slide)
- Headline: Predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
- One-liner to say in calls: "Redwood moves the burden of inference reliability and cost optimization off your platform team while giving you deployment choices and observability to own SLAs."
- Talking tip: Lead with a customer pain: "Are you seeing unpredictable token costs or tail latency spikes when traffic bursts?"

Slide 2: Where Redwood fits in stack (visual placeholder)
- Short bullets describing: runtime (GPU-optimized serving), orchestration, control plane, and console/observability
- Field note: Emphasize same API across hosted/dedicated/private — makes vendor lock-in and migration easier.

Slide 3: Typical buyer personas and triggers
- Personas: ML Platform Lead (cost + throughput), Product Manager (feature velocity), SRE (reliability/SLAs), Security/Compliance (data isolation)
- Triggers: unpredictable inference spend, outage during big events, need for on-prem/VPC, expectation of <100ms p50 generation for small prompts

Slide 4: Top 5 win themes (short bullets for quick memorize)
1) Predictable economics: batching, cache, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token spend (show % ranges TBD by Pricing)
2) Deployment flexibility: host now, private later — same API, same rollouts
3) Reliability & graceful degradation: policy routing & model fallbacks keep product online
4) Observability & ops: token-level cost, per-route latency, regression alerts tied to prompt sets
5) Enterprise readiness: KMS, audit logs, and SLA-backed dedicated pools

Slide 5: Quick metrics to drop in meetings (placeholders)
- Typical result statements (work with Applied ML to validate): "20-60% cost improvement after enabling KV cache and left-shift batching for chat workloads"
- "P99 latency reduced by 30% after runtime kernel optimizations for our verified models"
- Field note: Replace numbers with customer-specific benchmarks when possible.

One-pager Battlecard (single page rapid reference)
- Elevator: Redwood Inference — predictable inference economics + unified runtime across environments.
- Top pain points we solve:
  * Surging token costs during promotions or new feature rollouts
  * Tail latency spikes with open-source models on unoptimized runtimes
  * Compliance needs for regulated data (require private deployments & KMS)
- Key differentiators to lean on:
  * Production-first runtime with automated batching and KV caching
  * Transparent performance profiles and rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback)
  * Dedicated capacity with SLA and predictable throughput

Competitor snapshot (short-form)
- Vendor A (managed API provider): + simple API, - less transparent pricing, - no private/offline option in most regions.
  * Rebuttal: "We offer self-serve hosted API for quick time-to-value, but also Dedicated and Private for teams that need capacity guarantees or air-gapped setups."
- Vendor B (self-hosted runtime OSS): + low model cost on paper, - heavy ops and no unified analytics.
  * Rebuttal: "OSS runtimes can be cost-effective but they shift heavy maintenance and observability burden onto your team. Redwood provides the runtime innovations + ops tooling as a managed layer or private control plane."
- Vendor C (cloud managed endpoints): + tight cloud integration, - pricing variability and limited model catalog.
  * Rebuttal: "If you need multi-cloud/region routing and predictable unit economics, Redwood’s smart routing + cost controls are designed for that use case."

Objections and scripted replies (field-tested style)
- "We can just tune open-source LLMs in-house."
  * Reply: "Tuning and inference optimization are one part — but productionizing (autoscaling, debug for tail latency, regression monitoring, secure private rollouts) is where teams spend months. Redwood accelerates that timeline and provides SLO guardrails."
- "Your pricing looks high vs raw GPU cost."
  * Reply: "Compare total cost of ownership: infra ops, engineering time, risk of outages, and lost revenue from late production bugs. We also systematically reduce per-token spend via batching/caching so unit economics typically improve."
- "We need on-prem — how private is private?"
  * Reply: "We offer a private control plane that can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem package; keys never leave your KMS if you require it. Happy to pull in Security for a deeper technical runbook."

Proof points & short customer stories (placeholders to replace with PD/CS quotes)
- Retail customer X: cut inference spend by ~35% by enabling cache + smaller quantized model for recommendations pipeline (internal case id: CS-332).
- Fintech Y: met compliance by deploying Redwood Private into a dedicated VPC with HSM-backed KMS and audit trail.

Field playbook: discovery checklist (quick scan for ops signals)
- Ask: "How do you currently measure per-route token cost?"
- Ask: "Have you experienced tail-latency incidents in production? frequency and impact?"
- Ask: "Is there a need to keep data/keys inside your network or a requirement for air-gapped deployments?"
- Red flags that escalate to Solutions Eng:
  * Customer has strict <5ms tail-latency requirement for sub-token operations
  * Complex multi-region compliance boundaries requiring on-prem footprint

Demo suggestions (what to show in an ops-focused demo)
- Console: per-route token cost waterfall, latency distribution, model rollouts with canary metrics
- Live: enable KV cache for a sample chat flow and show p50/p95 before/after
- Backstage: quick peek at routing policy where we route to a cheaper quantized variant when budget exceeded

Open TODOs (action items before we ship to AE team)
- [ ] Get final cost improvement ranges from Pricing + Applied ML (owner: Marcelo)
- [ ] Add 2-3 validated customer quotes (owner: CS)
- [ ] Security: update private deployment checklist with HSM/KMS flows (owner: Elena)
- [ ] Convert slides into a short 6-slide deck for SE demo (owner: Riley)

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet for technical SEs
- Runtime optimizations we can call out:
  * Continuous batching: combines inbound requests safely to reduce GPU utilization
  * KV/prefix caching: keeps common context in memory to avoid recomputation
  * Quantization profiles: trade accuracy vs cost, we recommend model-specific presets
- Integration touchpoints: SDKs, REST API endpoint examples, rollout config snippet (link to repo in linked artifacts)

Notes to self (messy, keep):
- Keep language plain — field likes short, crisp lines.
- Need a separate one-pager focused on "Platform Cost Conversation" for partner AEs.
- Resist the urge to have too many numbers — customers will want to see comparisons to their baselines.

--- end of draft v2 ---

Please review and add customer-validated metrics or short quotes inline. Once Applied ML + Pricing sign off, I'll move to in_review and create a condensed 6-slide deck for SE demos.
